title: The Fed's 25-or-50-point September decision

market.proposition: The Fed decreases rates by at least 50 basis points after its September 2024 meeting.

events.headline: Global markets fall as weak US data and yen carry-trade unwinding raise growth fears
events.plausibleImpact: A sudden risk-off episode and recession concern could make traders expect the Fed to front-load easing, including a 50-point opening cut.
events.caveat: The selloff also reflected Bank of Japan policy and leveraged positioning; attribution to the Fed contract is plausible, not proven.

events.headline: July CPI confirms continued disinflation
events.plausibleImpact: Lower inflation gives policymakers room to respond more forcefully to labor-market weakness.
events.caveat: The report supported easing but did not by itself determine a 50-point first move.

events.headline: Powell says the time has come for policy to adjust
events.plausibleImpact: The explicit pivot confirms that easing is coming and leaves the opening move size as the central uncertainty.
events.caveat: A September cut was already widely anticipated before the speech.

events.headline: August payrolls are softer, with downward revisions, while unemployment edges lower
events.plausibleImpact: Softer revisions support a larger cut, while the lower unemployment rate reduces pressure for an emergency-sized move.
events.caveat: This was a mixed report and should be presented as genuinely ambiguous.

events.headline: August core CPI runs firmer than expected
events.plausibleImpact: Firmer core inflation weakens the case for a half-point first cut immediately after the meeting.
events.caveat: Labor-market risk and later policy communication remained relevant.

ending.text: The FOMC cut the target range by 50 basis points; the exact contract resolved YES. Keep this reveal separate from the five scored cards.
